You are given a Prize-Collecting Traveling Salesman Problem (PCTSP) instance.
The input describes a depot and a set of locations, each with coordinates, a prize for visiting, and a penalty if it is not visited. There is also a required minimum total prize that must be collected.

You will receive the instance in the following format:
{{INSTANCE_INPUT}}

Your task is to propose a single tour that starts and ends at the depot, collects at least the required total prize, and aims to minimize the overall objective (which combines tour length with penalties for unvisited locations).

Return your decision in **exactly** this JSON format:
```json
{
  "solution": [depot_id, location_id, ..., depot_id]
}
```
Here, `solution` is the visiting order of node identifiers, starting and ending at the depot. Use exactly the same node identifiers as in the input. Do not include explanations or extra keys.

part12.1: Someone in charge of the grocery vans has to plan one closed loop out of the depot, choosing which local stores to hit so the total expected restock meets the target quantity. The trade-off is clear: skipping a store costs a penalty, and every mile costs in distance, so the winner is the loop that makes the sum of miles driven plus penalties as small as possible. The loop must start and end at the depot, visit each chosen store only once, and collect enough restock from the visited stops. The specific store numbers, travel distances and penalties appear below.
part12.2: I run the mobile clinic and need to plan one continuous loop that leaves the clinic, stops at some farms to pick up booked vet appointments, and comes back to the clinic. The decision is which farms to include on that single circuit so the total number of appointments (or health coverage) collected hits a required target. A good plan keeps the driving time low but also avoids big fines for farms that get skipped — the score for any candidate route is simply the total drive time plus the penalties charged for farms left out. No farm should be visited more than once and the route must start and end at the clinic. The specific farm locations, penalties, appointment values and the target coverage are shown below.

The trade-off is simple: choose stops so the route is short but also so missed blocks don’t cost too much in lost sales — the “score” for any plan is just total miles driven plus the sum of lost‑sales penalties for blocks skipped, and a smaller score is better. The trip must be a single loop (no visiting blocks twice) and must bring in at least the required sales. Concrete details about the blocks, sales, and penalties are shown below.

contexts.text: [BASELINE] Canonical task wording.

As the grocery fleet manager, plan a single closed loop that departs from and returns to the depot, visiting a subset of neighborhood stores so that the total expected restock amount meets the required target while keeping the sum of driving distance and penalties for stores you skip as small as possible.

As the mobile clinic coordinator, map one continuous circuit from the clinic and back that visits chosen farms to collect vet appointments until a target health coverage is reached, minimizing the combined travel time and the fines or service penalties for any farms left out.

As an ice cream vendor, design a round trip that starts and ends at your truck garage and visits selected blocks to reach the needed sales target, with the aim of minimizing total route length plus lost sales penalties for blocks you do not stop at.

As the volunteer donation organizer, lay out a single looping route from the charity center that calls on certain donor houses until the pickup total meets the campaign target, minimizing overall travel cost together with disappointment or contractual penalties for skipped donors.

As the city streetlight inspector, create one continuous inspection tour beginning and ending at headquarters that visits chosen lamp posts to accumulate the required inspection priority score, while keeping the total roadway distance plus penalties for uninspected posts as low as possible.

As the photographer running a pop up business, plan a single circular route from your studio and back that visits selected meetup locations to achieve a minimum bookings target, minimizing the sum of travel expense and missed-session penalties for locations you omit.

As the pharmacy delivery coordinator, schedule a single round trip that leaves and returns to the pharmacy to visit patient homes until the medicines delivered meet the required quota, with the objective of minimizing driving cost plus regulatory or customer penalties for undelivered stops.

As the recycling program supervisor, design one continuous loop from the depot that stops at chosen neighborhood drop bins to collect enough recyclables to hit the target weight, minimizing the total route distance plus fines for bins you skip.

As the billboard maintenance manager, plan a single circuit that begins and ends at the operations office and inspects selected billboards to reach the required maintenance coverage, aiming to minimize total travel expense plus contractual penalties for billboards not visited.

As the field research lead, design a single sampling tour that starts and returns to base visiting chosen sites to gather at least the required data value, while minimizing the overall travel effort combined with penalties for unvisited sample sites.

As the regional sales manager, plan one continuous sales route from the office and back that calls on selected boutiques to reach a target order volume, minimizing the sum of travel mileage and lost-commission penalties for boutiques you skip.

As the librarian organizing the bookmobile, create a single loop that departs from and returns to the library visiting selected community drop boxes to collect enough returns to meet the target, with the goal of minimizing driving distance plus overdue or service penalties for boxes you miss.

As the mobile car detailer, schedule a single circuit from your shop that visits chosen customer addresses to reach the required booking revenue, minimizing the combined travel time and cancellation or refund penalties for customers you do not serve.

As the public health coordinator, plan a single round trip that starts and ends at the health center and visits selected neighborhoods to meet a minimum expected donor total for a blood drive, minimizing travel cost together with the penalties for communities not visited.

As the university admissions officer, map one continuous recruitment tour from campus that returns to campus visiting selected schools to reach the required prospective student contact total, with the aim of minimizing total travel expense plus outreach penalties for schools you do not visit.

As the pest control dispatcher, design a single looping route from the depot that treats chosen properties to achieve the required infestation mitigation score, minimizing the overall travel cost plus penalties for properties left untreated.

As the lab logistics manager, plan a single closed circuit from the laboratory that collects samples from selected clinics until the sample count meets the required threshold, minimizing the sum of courier travel time and penalties for clinics whose samples are not picked up.

As the marketing campaign manager, create a single promotional tour that departs from and returns to headquarters visiting selected event booths to reach a target audience exposure, minimizing route distance plus missed-opportunity penalties for booths you skip.

As the landscape business owner, arrange a single circular route from your yard that stops at chosen gardens to secure enough project value to meet your required target, while minimizing total driving distance together with penalties for clients you do not visit.

As a local courier, plan a single route that starts and ends at the central hub to visit a selection of customer addresses so you reach the required total value of parcel pickups while keeping the driving distance low and accounting for financial penalties for any pickup locations you skip.

As the museum outreach coordinator, design a single loop beginning and ending at the storage room to restock selected galleries until the needed cumulative restocking value is met, minimizing walking and transport effort plus added costs for galleries left unvisited.

As a neighborhood fundraiser, map out one continuous walking circuit from the community center and back that visits chosen houses to collect enough pledges to meet the campaign target while keeping your total travel and the expected loss from skipped houses as small as possible.

As a field service engineer, organize a single trip that departs from and returns to the office to attend selected client sites so you resolve the necessary total number of priority issues, minimizing travel expenses combined with compensation costs for clients you do not visit.

As a mobile library coordinator, create a single delivery round that starts and ends at the branch to bring requested books to a selection of pickup lockers until you achieve the required distribution quota while minimizing route length plus penalties for lockers left unserviced.

As an urban gardener supervisor, schedule a single maintenance tour beginning and ending at the depot to tend selected community plots until you meet the required total upkeep score while minimizing travel between plots plus fines for neglected plots.

As an antiques buyer, plot a single buying trip that leaves from and returns to your shop to visit a selection of sellers so you acquire at least the required total appraisal value while keeping mileage and the loss from skipped sellers as low as possible.

As a promotional route planner, craft one continuous street circuit that starts and finishes at the company van to stop at chosen stores until you secure the required total promotional placements while minimizing driving time plus penalties for stores you skip.

As a municipal inspector, lay out a single inspection loop from the office and back that visits selected properties so the inspected properties reach the mandated total inspection weight while minimizing travel costs plus the official penalties for properties not inspected.

As a photojournalist, arrange one round trip departing from and returning to the newsroom to photograph selected events so you meet the required editorial coverage value while minimizing travel distance plus the editorial cost of missed events.

As a florist delivering seasonal arrangements, plan a single delivery circuit that starts and returns to the shop to visit chosen customers so you fulfill the required total order value while minimizing delivery mileage plus compensation for any unserved customers.

As a concert promoter traveling between venues, devise one continuous tour that leaves from and returns to the office to secure chosen venues until you reach the required total booking value while keeping travel expense plus penalties for unscheduled venues as small as possible.

As a solar technician, schedule a single service route beginning and ending at the depot to attend selected rooftops so the installed capacity inspected meets the required total while minimizing drive time plus contractual penalties for sites you omit.

As a mobile pet clinic coordinator, plan one circular route from the clinic van and back that visits selected neighborhoods so you achieve the required total of services provided while minimizing travel effort together with the cost implications of neighborhoods you do not serve.

As a bicycle courier handling errand runs, organize one continuous ride that starts and ends at the bike depot to visit selected drop points so you collect the required total earnings while keeping pedal time and the penalties for missed stops as low as possible.

As an emergency kit distributor for a relief organization, plan one single trip leaving from and returning to headquarters to supply chosen shelters so you reach the required total distribution amount while minimizing travel distance plus the expected harm cost from shelters not served.

As a market researcher conducting in person interviews, design one uninterrupted route from the office and back that visits selected respondents so the cumulative survey value meets the required target while minimizing travel and the penalty for skipped respondents.

As a seasonal decorator installing displays, lay out a single installation circuit that starts at and returns to the storage yard to visit selected storefronts until you reach the required total display impact while minimizing transit distance plus fees for stores left unadorned.

Design a single loop that departs from and returns to the sales office to call on selected clients so the expected revenue meets the campaign requirement, minimizing travel expenses together with losses from clients not visited.

Choose a single circuit that leaves from and comes back to the garage to service a subset of machines so the total repair value reaches the required level, while minimizing total travel time plus penalties for machines left unserviced.

Map out a single guided itinerary that begins and finishes at the ticket desk to include a selection of exhibits so the accumulated visitor interest meets the museum target, keeping walking distance and the cost of skipped exhibits as small as possible.

Create a single delivery circuit that begins and returns to the distribution hub to serve a subset of subscribers so the collected subscription value meets the required amount, while minimizing delivery mileage together with penalties for missed deliveries.

Pick a single loop that originates from and returns to the courier locker to collect parcels at chosen pickup points so the total pickup value meets the operational target, minimizing riding time plus penalties for locations skipped.

Plan a single trip that departs from and comes back to the depot to treat selected properties so the combined treatment value meets the required threshold, keeping total driving cost and the costs for untreated properties as small as possible.

Schedule a single circuit that starts and returns to the clinic to reach selected community sites so vaccination impact meets the required target, and minimize travel hours together with penalties for sites that are not visited.

Plan a single busking loop that departs from and comes back to the starting street corner to play at selected spots so donations meet the daily target, minimizing walking distance and the opportunity cost from locations not performed at.

Plot a single field loop that begins and ends at base camp to sample a subset of sites so accumulated sample value meets the mission requirement, while minimizing transit distance plus penalties for unsampled locations.

Create a single rotation that starts and finishes at the depot to install meters at selected houses so total installation value reaches the required quota, minimizing driving cost together with penalties for houses left uninstalled.

Arrange a single circuit that sets out from and returns to the hotel to photograph chosen landmarks so the total photo value meets editorial needs, keeping travel expenses plus penalties for landmarks not covered as low as possible.

Map a single run that starts and ends at the store to deliver to some customer addresses so collected order value meets the target, while minimizing driving distance and penalties for orders not delivered.

Choose a single maintenance tour that leaves from and returns to the yard to service selected streetlights so total service value meets the minimum required, and keep travel cost plus the consequences of lights left unserviced as small as possible.

Design a single vending circuit that starts and ends at the storage unit to set up at chosen spots so projected sales reach the required amount, minimizing transit costs plus lost revenue from skipped locations.

Plan a single walk that begins and finishes at the kennel to exercise selected client dogs so total health benefit meets the required standard, minimizing walking distance and penalties for dogs not taken out.

item_fields.name: y

item_fields.name: penalty

item_fields.name: prize

item_fields.name: prize

item_fields.name: penalty

global_fields.name: num_nodes

item_fields.name: node_id

item_fields.name: x

item_fields.name: y

item_fields.name: prize

item_fields.name: penalty

item_fields.scenario_description: Y coordinate of the site (in the same planar units used for distance calculations); together with x_coord locates the site for computing travel distance between sites and the base camp.

item_fields.name: prize
item_fields.scenario_description: The amount of scientific/sample value collected by visiting this site; visiting adds this value to the tour's accumulated total toward the required_sample_total.

item_fields.name: penalty
item_fields.scenario_description: Penalty cost incurred if this site is not visited on the planned loop; the objective to minimize is travel distance plus the sum of unsampled_penalties for all skipped sites.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of locations in the instance, including the depot and all candidate houses; used to know how many location entries to expect.

global_fields.name: depot
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the depot location where the rotation both starts and finishes (the crew home base/vehicle origin).

global_fields.name: required_prize
global_fields.scenario_description: Minimum total installation value that must be collected on the single loop (sum of selected houses' installation values) to meet the quota.

item_fields.name: node_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this location entry (a house or the depot); referenced when building the single route of visits.

item_fields.name: x
item_fields.scenario_description: X coordinate of the location on the plane used to compute driving distances for route cost calculations.

item_fields.name: y
item_fields.scenario_description: Y coordinate of the location on the plane used to compute driving distances for route cost calculations.

item_fields.name: prize
item_fields.scenario_description: Value gained by installing a meter at this house; contributions from visited houses sum toward the required_installation_value.

item_fields.name: penalty
item_fields.scenario_description: Penalty cost incurred if this house is not visited on the rotation; unvisited houses add their skip_penalty to the route objective.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of locations in the instance, counting the hotel (the start/finish) plus all candidate landmarks to photograph. Used to understand the size of the route selection problem.

global_fields.name: depot
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the hotel node where the single photo run must start and end. This node is the depot for the loop and is not a landmark to be skipped for prize purposes.

global_fields.name: required_prize
global_fields.scenario_description: Minimum cumulative photo value that must be collected by the chosen loop of landmarks to satisfy the magazine’s editorial requirement.

item_fields.name: node_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for a location, either the hotel or a specific landmark that can be visited for photos.

item_fields.name: x
item_fields.scenario_description: X coordinate of the location on the map (used to compute travel distance/cost between locations).

item_fields.name: y
item_fields.scenario_description: Y coordinate of the location on the map (used to compute travel distance/cost between locations).

item_fields.name: prize
item_fields.scenario_description: Editorial value gained by photographing this location if it is included in the loop; these values sum to meet the required_total_photo_value.

item_fields.name: penalty
item_fields.scenario_description: Penalty cost incurred if this location is not visited on the single loop (represents the editorial or opportunity cost of omitting the landmark).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of locations in this delivery planning instance, including the store (the depot) and all customer addresses. Used to understand the size of the problem.

global_fields.name: depot
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the store where the single trip starts and ends. This node is the depot for the outbound-and-back loop.

global_fields.name: required_prize
global_fields.scenario_description: Minimum total order value that must be collected on the trip. The selected set of customer visits must have summed order values at least this target.

item_fields.name: node_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for a specific location (either the store or a customer address) used to reference stops when building a route.

item_fields.name: x
item_fields.scenario_description: X coordinate of the location on the map (in the same units used to compute driving distance). Coordinates are used to calculate miles driven between stops for the route cost.

item_fields.name: y
item_fields.scenario_description: Y coordinate of the location on the map (in the same units used to compute driving distance). Together with map_x, used to compute distance between locations.

item_fields.name: prize
item_fields.scenario_description: Monetary value of the customer's order that is collected if the location is visited. The sum of collected order_values must meet or exceed the target_sales_amount.

item_fields.name: penalty
item_fields.scenario_description: Penalty cost incurred if this customer address is not visited on the trip. For any candidate route, the total score equals miles driven plus the sum of skip_penalties for all unvisited customers.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of locations the crew considers, including the yard (depot) plus all streetlights that could be serviced on the tour.

global_fields.name: depot
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the yard where the maintenance crew starts and ends the single looped route.

global_fields.name: required_prize
global_fields.scenario_description: Minimum cumulative service value that the crew must obtain by visiting selected streetlights during the tour.

item_fields.name: node_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for a specific streetlight or the yard node; used to reference which locations may be visited or skipped.

item_fields.name: x
item_fields.scenario_description: X coordinate (map or planar) of the streetlight or yard used to compute travel distance between locations for the route.

item_fields.name: y
item_fields.scenario_description: Y coordinate (map or planar) of the streetlight or yard used together with x_coord to determine travel distances for the tour.

item_fields.name: prize
item_fields.scenario_description: The value or benefit gained by servicing this streetlight (contributes toward meeting the required_service_value if the light is visited).

item_fields.name: penalty
item_fields.scenario_description: Cost or consequence incurred if this streetlight is not included on the tour; added to the objective when the light is left unserviced.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of locations in the instance, counting the storage unit (depot) plus all possible vending spots. Use this to size arrays and iterate over all nodes.

global_fields.name: depot
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the storage unit where the vendor starts and ends the single circuit. This node is the loop origin/terminus for the planned vending route.

global_fields.name: required_prize
global_fields.scenario_description: Minimum total projected sales that must be collected from the visited spots on the route. The chosen circuit must visit enough locations so the sum of their projected sales meets or exceeds this target.

item_fields.name: node_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this location (either the storage unit or a vending spot). Refer to this id when specifying which places are visited in the circuit.

item_fields.name: x
item_fields.scenario_description: X coordinate of the location on the plane (used with coord_y to compute travel distances and thus transit cost between locations).

item_fields.name: y
item_fields.scenario_description: Y coordinate of the location on the plane (used with coord_x to compute travel distances and thus transit cost between locations).

item_fields.name: prize
item_fields.scenario_description: Projected sales (revenue) the vendor expects to collect by setting up at this spot. The sum of projected_sales over visited locations contributes toward meeting the required_sales_target.

item_fields.name: penalty
item_fields.scenario_description: Revenue forfeited (penalty) if this location is not included in the route. The solver adds these penalties for all unvisited spots to the travel cost when computing the objective to minimize.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of locations on the route, including the kennel. This counts the kennel plus all client addresses that could be visited.

global_fields.name: depot
global_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the kennel location (the start and end of the single walk loop). This node is the walk origin/return point.

global_fields.name: required_prize
global_fields.scenario_description: Minimum total health benefit that must be achieved by the set of dogs walked on the outing. The chosen tour must visit dogs whose summed health_benefit meets or exceeds this value.

item_fields.name: node_id
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for a location (either the kennel or a client address). Used to reference which client/kennel is visited or skipped.

item_fields.name: x
item_fields.scenario_description: X coordinate of the location on the map used to compute walking distance (e.g., map/mile coordinates). Distances between locations are derived from these coordinates.

item_fields.name: y
item_fields.scenario_description: Y coordinate of the location on the map used to compute walking distance (paired with x_coord).

item_fields.name: prize
item_fields.scenario_description: Health benefit value gained by taking that client's dog on the walk (contributes toward the required_health_benefit). The kennel/depot will typically have zero.

item_fields.name: penalty
item_fields.scenario_description: Monetary penalty (or charge) the service incurs if that client's dog is not included on the walk. Unvisited clients add their missed_walk_penalty to the total objective.
